Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

the finger noun

the obscene gesture

also give someone the finger, flip someone off, flip the bird, middle finger (obscene gesture), rude gesture, obscene gesture

classical

Mart. 6.70.5 (Lewis & Short s.v. impudīcus)
Traupman 315

digitus impudīcus

the middle finger, as an obscene gesture

Literally “the shameless finger”: the Romans used the middle finger as we do. Lewis & Short (s.v. digitus) gives it three names: medius, īnfāmis and impudīcus.

Other words

  • digitus īnfāmis — the middle finger (“the disreputable finger”)

    also used · classical · Pers. 2.33 (Lewis & Short s.v. īnfāmis)

  • medium unguem ostendere — give the finger, show utter contempt

    also used · classical · Juv. 10.53 (Lewis & Short s.v. unguis)

    Literally “show the middle nail”.

See also index finger, finger, dirty talk.

SourcesLewis & Short: impudicus · Lewis & Short: infamis · Lewis & Short: unguis · Lewis & Short: digitus
